title: The Trust Team Welcomes Two Editors
summary: It is an important moment for trust in what we do. Confidence in the news media has been declining for years. We are awash in A.I. slop, partisan news and the rise of influencers.
body_markdown:
Chloe Shakin and Jillian Eugenios will help highlight the how and why of our journalism. Read more from assistant managing editor Patrick Healy and deputy editor Mike Abrams.


It is an important moment for trust in what we do. Confidence in the news media has been declining for years. We are awash in A.I. slop, partisan news and the rise of influencers. Many people trust The Times, but we’ve found that they also say they want to understand us better. Others remain skeptical of us and unclear about the work we put in to ensure fairness and accuracy.


The more we work to bolster trust in The Times, the more we realize what we can accomplish with a slightly larger team. So we’re pleased to welcome two editors to our fold: Jillian Eugenios and Chloe Shakin.


When we started working on videos last fall, we were starting from a blank slate. Then we met Jillian, who had worked with the newsroom’s Reporter Video team. We brought her on as a temporary senior producer for Trust and haven’t looked back. She quickly built a workflow while showing herself to be an ideas generator and collaborative editor, all of which led the way to a


[string](https://www.nytimes.com/video/insider/100000011030047/our-top-editor-on-subpoenas-of-times-journalists.html)[of](https://www.nytimes.com/video/insider/100000010942319/how-our-theater-reporter-makes-his-tony-award-predictions.html)[well](https://www.nytimes.com/video/insider/100000010994126/what-can-a-poll-tell-us.html) –


[received](https://www.nytimes.com/video/insider/100000010994124/why-are-we-polling-now.html)[Times Insider videos](https://www.nytimes.com/video/insider/100000011077518/how-were-covering-an-identity-crisis-in-politics.html) .


Now we’re removing the temporary tag from her title. She’ll work with our team full time while reporting to Solana Pyne, the newsroom’s director of Video.


“Jillian brings thoughtful sensitivity to complex stories on tight deadlines and is an excellent collaborator, whether interviewing our journalists, communicating with the newsroom or wrangling production logistics,” Solana said. “I’m thrilled to have her on board.”


Before joining The Times, Jillian oversaw an award-winning social video team at NBC News focused on Gen Z audiences. She also worked at


[“Great Big Story,”](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCajXeitgFL-rb5-gXI-aG8Q) traveling the country and making short documentaries – projects that garnered an Emmy and a Gracie award. Earlier in her career, she was a reporter for CNN and for the “Today” show after getting her start in Sydney, Australia, where she worked at a free magazine for L.G.B.T.Q. community members.


Jillian is a graduate of the Craig Newmark Graduate School of Journalism at CUNY, where she studied business and economics reporting, and she also holds an M.F.A. in creative writing from the New School. Off the clock, she is a licensed New York City tour guide and a dabbler in ceramics.


Photo Credit: Earl W


Chloe will join us this fall as an assistant Trust editor, coming from the newsroom’s Audience team in London. She will take on a new role aimed at deepening engagement with both our audience and non-audience, including Times skeptics and critics, chiefly by developing an off-platform strategy for our work and a system for assessing reader questions and delivering feedback at scale.


Chloe brings formidable skills to the task. From London, she has promoted and explained our journalism on a wide range of coverage across social platforms: the 2024 U.S. election results, the wars in Gaza and Iran, the appointments of two British prime ministers, two Olympic Games in Europe and more. She also worked closely with the London Video team to stand up a new workflow to more quickly capitalize on trends, which resulted in some high-performing videos, including


[our most-viewed TikTok video](https://www.tiktok.com/@nytimes/video/7437415566719061290?utm_campaign=tt4d_open_api&utm_source=6997707748318117889) .


“Chloe is just the kind of editor you want on your team,” said Anna Dubenko, the newsroom’s Audience director. “She thinks across mediums and platforms, identifying opportunities and giving her colleagues sharp edits that make our framing better and help our journalism travel further.”


Chloe studied English and journalism at the University of Pennsylvania and joined The Times in 2017 as an intern on the Growth team, returning full time the following year. While on the business side, she received a master’s degree from Columbia University’s Graduate School of Journalism. She received a Pulitzer traveling fellowship, awarded to top members of the graduating class, which she spent reporting on maternal mental health care in Britain. Her reporting culminated in a


[narrative feature on postpartum psychosis](https://www.nytimes.com/2024/10/09/well/postpartum-psychosis-health-pregnancy-women.html) for Well that was selected as a Great Read and ran on A1. Chloe has also


[freelanced](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/24/well/menopause-melani-sanders-club.html) for several desks, including


[Well](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/18/well/skin-hair-picking-dermatillomania.html)[and](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/07/31/world/europe/transgender-children-health-study-uk-nhs.html)[International](https://www.nytimes.com/article/uk-liverpool-parade-car-crash.html) .


Raised on Long Island, Chloe is excited to return to her 516 area code after a few years of WhatsApp-ing from a +44 number — and, of course, reintegrating what used to be the N.Y.C. dollar slice into her weeknight rotation. In her spare time, she enjoys taking park runs (punctuated by stops to pet strangers’ dogs), thrift shopping and hosting dinners.


Chloe and Jillian will join Megan DiTrolio and Seth Carlson on our team to build on a growing portfolio of work designed to showcase the how and why of our journalism through videos, a newsletter, Times Insider pieces, round tables and more.


Please join us in congratulating them.


— Patrick and Mike
